rules: Label only what the website states. No outside knowledge. Copy quotes exactly. If pages disagree, record both as conflicting. If the site does not say, use not_found.
review_notes: Buffer describes itself elsewhere (About page) as a fully remote, distributed team with no single office ('scattered around the world'); the address used for headquarters is Buffer, Inc.'s registered/legal address as stated in its Terms of Use, not a described physical HQ office -- flagged as a judgment call. customers.industries left not_found because Buffer names customer *segments* (creators, small businesses, agencies, nonprofits, higher ed) but does not name specific verticals/industries. Named customers are homepage logos with no accompanying case-study quotes captured. Competitor list comes from Buffer's own /compare page, which explicitly names and contrasts against each competitor. B-51 (2026-09-27): customers.segments' evidence was originally a paraphrase description, not a literal quote; re-checked live and confirmed these six segment names are genuine short labels repeated on the homepage and in the site footer under a 'Made for' heading -- evidence updated to those exact labels.

evidence: Buffer offers more streamlined scheduling and analytics compared to Agorapulse's CRM focused features.
While eClincher provides automation options, Buffer stands out with its user-friendly interface and simplicity.
Hootsuite's broad functionality is matched by Buffer's focused, intuitive approach to social media scheduling and analytics.
While Later excels in Instagram marketing, Buffer provides a more holistic approach for managing multiple social platforms.
While Loomly focuses on approval workflows built for agencies, Buffer offers a simpler, more affordable way to plan and publish.
Meta Business Suite is limited to Facebook and Instagram, while Buffer offers streamlined scheduling and analytics across all your social media channels.
